title: Counterfactual Auditing of Bias in Open-Source Large Language Models for Clinical Triage
abstract: arXiv:2610.01963v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Emergency department (ED) triage is a high-stakes prioritization task in which demographic, socioeconomic, and system-context information may improperly influence acuity assignment. Although open-source large language models (LLMs) are increasingly considered for local and privacy-preserving clinical decision support, it remains unclear how counterfactual bias varies across model families, sizes, medical-domain models, and domain-adapted models. We present a comparative counterfactual audit of ten open-source LLMs for pediatric Emergency Severity Index (ESI) prediction. Starting from real and handbook-style clinical vignettes, we construct paired counterfactual variants that change only one injected demographic, socioeconomic, healthcare-access, behavioral, social, or system-context variable while holding the clinical presentation fixed. Models include Qwen2.5-7B, Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct, a QLoRA fine-tuned Qwen2.5-7B, MedGemma variants, Me

translated_title: 开源大语言模型在临床分诊中偏差的反事实审计
translated_abstract: 急诊科（ED）分诊是一项高风险的优先级排序任务，其中人口统计学、社会经济和系统环境信息可能会不当影响急症级别的判定。尽管开源大语言模型（LLM）越来越多地被考虑用于本地化和保护隐私的临床决策支持，但反事实偏差在不同模型家族、模型规模、医疗领域专用模型和领域适配模型之间的差异仍不清楚。我们对十个开源大语言模型在儿科急诊严重程度指数（ESI）预测方面进行了比较性反事实审计。从真实的和手册式临床病例描述出发，我们构建了配对的反事实变体，这些变体仅改变一个注入的人口统计学、社会经济、医疗可及性、行为、社会或系统环境变量，同时保持临床表现不变。模型包括Qwen2.5-7B、Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct、经QLoRA微调的Qwen2.5-7B、MedGemma变体等。
tldr: 该研究构建配对反事实病例对十个开源大语言模型在儿科急诊分诊预测中的偏差进行系统审计，揭示了人口统计、社会经济和医疗可及性等非临床变量对不同模型家族、规模及医疗领域适配模型分诊结果的不当影响。
en_tdlr: This study presents a comparative counterfactual audit of ten open-source LLMs for pediatric emergency triage prediction, revealing how injected demographic, socioeconomic, and healthcare-access variables improperly influence acuity assignment across different model families, sizes, and medical-domain adapted models.
